business_scope.primary_industry_name: Customs Clearance Brokerage and Bonded Transit Management

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of the Marshall Islands — Non-Resident Business Corporation (RMI BCA)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: U.S.-inspired common law statutory framework with customary land and traditional law overlay
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association with the United States of America (1986, as amended 2003) — investment, trade and fiscal treatment provisions
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus) — regional trade and investment framework
World Trade Organization accession instrument (2023) — GATS, TRIPS and trade facilitation commitments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act 1990 (RMI Revised Code, Title 26) read with the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2018 (AML/CFT Act, P.L. 2018-34) and the AML/CFT Regulations 2018; Beneficial Ownership Directive of the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) mandating 25% UBO disclosure through licensed registered agents; Customs Act 2007 (Title 43) and Customs Regulations licensing regime; Business License Act 1988 (Title 11)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified identity documents (passport and proof of residential address) of each UBO, director and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly authorized public notary in the document holder's country of domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the origin country is a Party) or, failing that, Consular Legalization at the nearest Marshall Islands diplomatic/consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and indirect ownership chart (Form BOR-2) commencing from the named shareholder to the ultimate natural person
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Marshall Islands licensed registered agent (TCSP) on behalf of the applicant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized by the TCSP and transmitted under RMI FIU-certified verified extract; apostille/consular legalization of any power-of-attorney execution pages required by source-country law

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or registry extract for every corporate direct shareholder and intermediate holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registrar or equivalent competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization chain

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank professional/reference letter covering counterparty due diligence trustworthiness for the proposed customs brokerage business
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated financial institution maintaining the prospective transferor/UBO relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank certification plus notarial attestation; apostille/consular chain not required where banker's signature is accepted by the RMI FIU guidance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney from the intended directors and UBOs in favor of the RMI resident registered agent for incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization of the certified execution page

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Risk-based mandatory customer due diligence under AML/CFT Act 2018 and Regulations: each UBO and authorized signatory must be screened against PEP databases, OFAC SDN/Consolidated List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU sanctions lists, and RMI domestic watchlist maintenance; enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies to foreign PEPs and politically exposed family members; enhanced monitoring and audit-trail retention apply for a medium-risk enhanced customs brokerage classification under ISIC 5229.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Corporate Registry — Name Reservation and Search Module, operated by the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Majuro Atoll
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory corporate denomination must be rendered in the Latin alphabet; English is the official registry language. No Marshallese-language transliteration requirement exists. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to any registered name, must include a corporate suffix ('Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', 'Company' or an acceptable abbreviation), and must be distinguishable on the RMI name index.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Registrar of Corporations within 10 business days using Form RMI-NAME-APP, attaching the name search certification and a written legal memorandum on distinguishability. The Registrar must issue a written determination within 15 business days. A further rejection may be challenged before the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands within 21 days under the Administrative Procedure Act (Title 6, Chapter 24); an alternative name may be simultaneously reserved without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible for Stage 1 statutory purposes: the BCA requires only a designated registered agent and a registered office for service of process, which may be the agent's address. However, for the ISIC 5229 licensed customs brokerage operation, RMI Customs and the Business License Act require either an in-country licensed customs broker or a demonstrably supervised local sub-agent maintaining records; a purely virtual office will not satisfy operational licensing requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Stage 1 estimated at 15% for a non-operating non-resident BC; risk escalates to 30–40% after customs broker license application and business license issuance, with AML/CFT supervisory inspections and unannounced Customs premises audits under the medium-risk-enhanced tier.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory corporate name search and 30-day name reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, RMI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff — BCA name reservation fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified name clearance / no-conflict letter (official registry extract)
Notarization and apostille/consular legalization bundle for UBO identity documents and powers of attorney (five-core-document package)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of approximately USD 150 per document package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, EU and RMI domestic sanctions screening and CDD file assembly (two UBOs, one director, one designated customs-broker officer)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for medium-risk enhanced onboarding

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent appointment, service-of-process facility and registry correspondence, year 1
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing annual market retainer, inclusive of AML/CFT Act TCSP record-keeping

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation AML/CFT legal opinion covering UBO piercing verdict and ISIC 5229 customs-brokerage licensing route
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External counsel admitted to practice in the Republic of the Marshall Islands
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee; prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-application consultation with a licensed RMI customs broker on operational substance and bonded transit management requirements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market consultation fee (non-refundable, credited against future cooperation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified international courier and secure e-document transmission for apostilled/legalized originals

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, as amended, principally Articles 1 through 4; applicable sections include Articles 101 (Articles of Incorporation), 103 (Registered Office and Agent), 108 (First Directors), and 109 (Bylaws). The foreign investor and non-resident ownership provisions are contained in Articles 13 and 17, together with the RMI Business License Law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro Atoll, MH.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for a non-resident Business Corporation; the Articles of Incorporation must declare the authorized capital structure and par value. There is no escrow deposit requirement under the Business Corporations Act; capital contributions are governed by the board's share subscription contracts and may be deferred.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the subscription for shares issued to the initial shareholders as recorded in the Articles of Incorporation; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation in the Republic of the Marshall Islands is adopted as the address maintained by the registered agent, and the registered agent is authorized to accept service of process; RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed: [Name], President; [Name], Secretary; and [Name], Treasurer, with authority to execute all filings, banking instructions, and customs brokerage license applications; RESOLVED, that the Corporation may incur reasonable costs and contracting expenses to obtain the operational business license and to open bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Non-Interference Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations – Name Reservation Desk, Majuro, RMI.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name reservation application through the RMI Online Registry Portal or by written submission to the Registrar. The proposed name must include a distinctive corporate identifier such as 'Limited' or 'Corporation' and must not be deceptively similar to any existing RMI entity. The Registrar will confirm name availability and reserve the name for a statutory period.
required_dossiers: Notarized identification documents of the incorporator
List of proposed directors and officers, if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, file an alternate name reservation or submit a notarized consent declaration from the prior name holder within ten business days; the Registrar will then review the corrected submission within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution, and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations or authorized registered agent in the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation on Form CBC-1 with the corporate name, registered office address, registered agent details, authorized share capital, par value, and lawful business purpose. The incorporator must execute the Articles before a notary public. Concurrently, approve the Bylaws by written consent of the incorporator to establish governance procedures for the first board meeting.
required_dossiers: Executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation (Form CBC-1)
Original notarized consent of the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency query, correct the identified item and re-file within 15 days; failure to cure within 30 days triggers a late processing fee and forfeiture of original filing order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Payment of Government Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cashier and Filing Office, RMI Registrar of Corporations; online payment portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Articles of Incorporation in triplicate together with the official filing fee of USD 250. Payment may be made by wire transfer, cashier's check, or approved electronic payment interface. Obtain a stamped receipt of filing and retain evidence of payment for the formation record.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation, three copies
Government filing fee payment receipt or wire confirmation
Power of attorney authorizing the filing agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment verification fails, the applicant must resubmit proof of funds from a recognized financial institution within five business days; otherwise, the filing is suspended and must be re-initiated with an updated application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of Corporations – Certificate Section, Ministry of Finance, Majuro, RMI.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful review and payment verification, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The registered agent's consent is recorded, and the statutory registered office address is confirmed. The Company is authorized to transact business as a domestic non-resident Business Corporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
Registered Agent Appointment and Consent Form (CBC-2)
Record of registered office address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a typographical or legal error, file a written request for certificate correction with supporting affidavit; the Registrar will reissue the certificate within ten business days. If the registered agent's appointment is rejected, file a substitute appointment form promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Share Subscription, and Corporate Governance Assembly
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretariat of the Corporation; filings to be recorded with the Registrar of Corporations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct the first board meeting by unanimous written consent or formal meeting. Adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution to accept share subscriptions, adopt the registered office, and appoint officers. Issue share certificates, open corporate bank accounts, and execute the operational authority for the customs brokerage license application.
required_dossiers: First Board Meeting Minutes or Unanimous Written Consent
Share certificates issued to initial shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the officers' statement, correct the officer information and resubmit Form BC-1 within 14 days; any administrative suspension resulting from registry delay is cured by payment of a reinstatement fee and submission of corrected documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: RMI Customs Service, Trade and Brokerage Division, Office of the Comptroller of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Broker License and Bonded Transit Operator Permit (Sub-Class 5229-03)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Registration and screening; full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not required for an office-only customs brokerage operation. If a bonded physical warehouse or container yard is established, the facility is elevated to Category A requiring a full EIA Report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No uncontrolled wastewater discharge is permitted; stormwater run-off must be managed to prevent contaminated discharge into adjacent waters. Any dry-port or bonded storage area must meet the Solid Waste Management Regulations 1996 for waste handling. Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in enclosed storage areas must remain below 500 ppm averaged over eight hours; particulate emissions, dust, noise, and transportation of sealed cargo must comply with the RMI Public Health and Safety Standards. Spill response and containment plan required for any fuel or chemical storage on site.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance Certificate from the Fire Safety Division, RMI Ministry of Interior; structural load and building use approval from the Ministry of Public Works for any bonded warehouse, transit shed, or cargo inspection area; occupational safety clearance from the RMI Occupational Safety and Health Office covering loading dock operations, customs seal verification, powered industrial truck use, and worker exposure to documentary chemical or fume hazards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenue and Taxation Office (RTO), Ministry of Finance, Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Corporate registration is administered by the Registrar of Corporations under the Business Corporations Act (BICA); customs declarations are processed by the Marshall Islands Customs Service (MICS) through the ASYCUDA World national single-window portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident Business Corporations are exempt from Marshall Islands income tax under the Income Tax Act and BICA Section 51; accordingly, no domestic TIN is statutorily required for such entities. A foreign-owned BC obtains corporate legal personality and a Certificate of Good Standing solely from the Registrar of Corporations. If a TIN is requested by banks or counterparties for FATCA/CRS or interbank due diligence, the entity may apply voluntarily to the RTO by submitting (i) Certificate of Incorporation, (ii) registered agent certificate, and (iii) a notarised declaration of non-resident status; RTO processing is typically completed within 5-10 business days and does not create or imply any tax liability.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone - Non-Resident Domestic Corporation: the MH_BC Business Corporation, not conducting trade or business in the Republic and deriving no income from Marshall Islands sources, is excluded from income tax, social security contributions, and withholding tax; it is also outside any indirect tax regime (no such regime exists). The only recurring state obligations are annual BICA franchise/registration fees payable to the Registrar of Corporations and the registered agent fee.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box, fiscal-transparency, or OECD hybrid-mismatch elections exist under Marshall Islands law. Entity classification is imposed by statute: a BC is a separate legal and taxable person; tax exemption is a legal consequence of non-resident status rather than an elective regime. The only practical options are structural, namely the maintenance of non-resident status (no domestic gross income and no permanent establishment in the Republic) and the designation of the registered office and agent. No CFC, hybrid-mismatch, or equivalent election forms apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST or general sales tax regime exists in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. The only indirect taxes are customs import duties, import excise taxes, and administrative service fees levied at the border under the Customs Revenue Act and related customs regulations. Customs brokerage services rendered by a non-resident BC are not subject to any indirect tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable: there is no VAT/GST registration threshold in the Republic. Customs registration obligations apply instead at a zero economic turnover threshold to importers, exporters, and customs brokers: any person performing customs clearance must hold a valid customs broker licence issued by the Marshall Islands Customs Service and must be registered in ASYCUDA World. This is a customs licensing requirement, not an indirect tax registration requirement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping mandate applies in the Marshall Islands. However, all customs declarations must be filed electronically through the ASYCUDA World single window operated by MICS, with automated broker interface/ACH connectivity for declaration submission, payment of applicable duties, and receipt of electronic release notifications. Commercial e-invoicing is governed by contractual and AML/record-keeping standards rather than by a government fiscal clearance system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in a VAT sense: the Marshall Islands has no VAT system, and therefore there is no 0% export VAT rate and no refund mechanism. Under customs law, exports from the Republic are duty-free and free of export taxes provided the goods are physically removed from the territory. A licensed customs brokerage house must file a valid export declaration in ASYCUDA World and evidence departure (port release and bill of lading) to obtain formal export status. Because the MH_BC is non-resident and offshore, its brokerage services have no territorial nexus to any indirect tax at all.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export entry filed and customs-approved in the ASYCUDA World single window)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill) evidencing physical export and the out-of-territory destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT credit confirmation) evidencing receipt of export consideration from abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Marshall Islands Customs Service conducts post-clearance audits and documentation reviews (records generally retained for 5 years). Because no VAT refund mechanism exists, the principal clawback exposure is the revocation of duty-free export status on shipments whose export documentation is inadequate, with resultant assessment of penalty duties, interest, forfeiture of goods, and fines under the Customs Revenue Act. Fraudulent declarations additionally expose the licensed brokerage to licence suspension or revocation and criminal liability for wilful evasion. The 180-day inward-remittance benchmark is applied as the internal repatriation and documentation deadline; although the Republic imposes no exchange controls, failure to evidence receipt of export proceeds within that window may trigger enhanced AML/CFT review by RMI-licensed banks and adverse audit findings, but cannot trigger an indirect-tax clawback because no indirect tax is levied in the Republic.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) maintains no independent central bank and no foreign exchange authority. Banking supervision is exercised by the Banking Commissioner acting through the Banking Commission under the Ministry of Finance, pursuant to the Banking Act 1991 and the Financial Institutions (AML/CFT) Regulations. Monetary denomination follows de jure adoption of the United States Dollar as the sole lawful currency under the Compact of Free Association, with USD cash management and clearing dependent on US Federal Reserve facilities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. Because the USD is the domestic legal tender, there is no separate local currency to convert, no exchange-control permit regime, no Central Bank approval for capital import or repatriation, and no restriction on profit remittance, shareholder loans, or liquidation proceeds. A non-resident Tax-Exempt Business Corporation that derives no RMI-source income is not subject to RMI income tax, the 3% gross receipts tax, or dividend withholding; statutory withholding (up to 15%) and the 3% gross receipts tax apply only to distributions sourced from RMI trade or business activity, which is avoided by a properly scoped customs brokerage fee structure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. RMI law imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation on export receipts or service revenues. Customs brokerage and bonded-transit management fees may be retained in USD in any licensed RMI bank or offshore account without declaration to the Ministry of Finance, subject only to record-keeping obligations under the AML/CFT Regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Marshall Islands (BMI) - Majuro Head Office
Bank Pacific LLC (formerly Bank of Guam - Republic of the Marshall Islands Branch)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary account solution. The RMI has no domestic Electronic Money Institution licensing regime and no foreign EMI passporting framework. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Revolut Business) cannot issue a local RMI account, provide an RMI routing number, or settle payments to the RMI Customs Service or port authorities. Such platforms are structurally viable only as a supplementary collection conduit for freight deposits or small client prepayments, with all funds subsequently swept by SWIFT MT103 into the licensed RMI bank account; legal constraints include source-of-funds latency, absence of local dispute jurisdiction, and the licensed bank's overriding obligation to look through to the underlying payer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for newly formed non-resident entities. All directors, beneficial owners, and authorised signatories must attend an in-person KYC interview at the relevant branch in Majuro or Ebeye, or before a bank officer attending at the RMI registered agent's office. The Banking Commission's AML guidance treats face-to-face verification as the presumptive standard. Remote opening is permitted only for established credit relationships, government-owned entities, or publicly listed financial institutions under enhanced due diligence; a newly incorporated Tax-Exempt BC without prior banking history cannot be opened remotely.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer-share legacy history, nominee shareholder structure, or incomplete register of members flagged during corporate verification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registrar-issued certificate of good standing; registered agent certificate confirming the share register carries no bearer certificates; full member register; nominee declaration identifying beneficial owner, settlor, and protector; board resolution ratifying share structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident exempt company with no local payroll or operational substance applying for a customs brokerage account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid RMI Customs Broker License issued under the Customs Act naming the corporate entity and its qualifying licensed individual; registered agent undertaking; physical office lease in Majuro; RMI Social Security Administration payroll filings for the resident customs manager; board resolution approving the local operational mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound capital injection from a mixed-jurisdiction holding chain relying on tax-haven intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds file for each subscribing shareholder; audited financial statements or certified bank statements of the parent entity; full organisational chart of the holding chain; independent counsel legal opinion confirming tax-exempt status and verifying the absence of proceeds-of-crime nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party duty disbursement flows (customs payments made on behalf of clients) characterised as money-laundering layering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CFT programme and institutional risk assessment filed with the Banking Commission; client onboarding file with executed customs brokerage mandate agreements; itemised duty-payment schedules cross-referenced to ASYCUDA World declarations; monthly two-year settlement ledger reconciled with the RMI Customs Service and port authority receipts; internal transaction-monitoring policy covering all fiduciary escrow disbursements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing uses SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for correspondent legs) to the RMI bank's US correspondent account maintained with a US clearing bank (e.g., Bank of Hawaii or Bank of Guam), with final credit to the beneficiary's account at the Majuro branch. Field 50K must show the founding shareholder; field 59 the BC name and account number; field 70 the purpose narrative: 'Capital subscription - issue of share capital, no RMI-source income'. The RMI imposes no exchange-control filing, but the receiving bank requires a share-subscription resolution, updated share register entry, and source-of-funds documentation. For internal policy clarity, the bank accepts IMF BPM6 purpose-code annotation (equity injection) where the narrative is mapped; no separate approval from the Ministry of Finance is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearance rails are exclusively USD-denominated. Primary channels: (i) SWIFT MT103 wires for overseas correspondents, shipping lines, freight forwarders, surveyors, and foreign customs-broker sub-agents; (ii) local ACH/RTGS settlement through the RMI clearing house for domestic disbursements, including customs duty transfers to the RMI Customs Service and bonded-warehouse fees; (iii) US Automated Broker Interface (ABI) and ACE transmissions for US-bound cargo entry, executed through the bank's US correspondent relationship; (iv) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) and standby bank guarantees for bonded transit collateral. Every outgoing duty payment must reference the relevant ASYCUDA World declaration number to permit automated reconciliation by the RMI Customs Service.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR and USD/AUD deliverable forwards and spot contracts executed through US or Australian clearing banks; no RMI licensing restriction applies to a non-financial BC engaging in trade-related hedging
USD/JPY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) transacted via an international bank with corresponding confirmation to the RMI account bank for Asian freight-leg settlement
AUD/USD and NZD/USD cross-currency swaps for bonded-transit route funding and port-fee liabilities
Plain-vanilla interest-rate swaps on USD floating-rate facilities provided by Bank of Marshall Islands, subject to bank credit approval and board derivative-authorisation policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Government Franchise Fee Payment (Corporate Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Commercial Division, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the anniversary month of incorporation; if a different fiscal year is adopted, within 60 days after the close of such fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 200 per month or fraction thereof; continued default for 30 days after written notice triggers administrative dissolution and strike-off from the Register of Corporations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Customs Brokerage Licence Annual Renewal (Licensed Customs Clearance Brokerage House)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands Customs Service, Ministry of Finance and Banking
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March or the anniversary date of the original licence, as specified in the Customs Brokerage Licensing Regulations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate suspension of brokerage operating authority; accrual of USD 100 per day penalty; revocation of licence after 60 days of non-renewal and disqualification from reapplying for 12 months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent under the Business Corporations Act; available to the Registrar of Corporations upon demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days before the Annual Report filing date; a signed declaration from each member and director required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registered agent is barred from effecting further corporate changes; the Registrar may issue a notice of default, leading to administrative penalties not exceeding USD 1,000 and possible strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Non-Resident Tax Status Declaration and Exemption Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands Revenue and Statistics Office (RASO), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the Annual Report filing, or by 31 March if the entity has not otherwise filed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of tax-exempt non-resident status for the taxable year; retroactive income tax assessment at the standard corporate rate of 3% on worldwide income derived from RMI sources; late filing interest and penalties apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Register Audit Certificate (Register Audit and Compliance Attestation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations (submitted by the registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be submitted together with the Annual Report, certifying that the Register of Members, Register of Directors, and Minute Book are physically available and up to date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Irregularities reported by the registered agent give rise to an administrative inquiry; failure to correct within 60 days may result in corporate dissolution or disqualification of the registered agent.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit for a non-resident Business Corporation unless (i) the company is listed or public, (ii) the company is a licensed bank, insurance, or trust entity, (iii) the RMI Customs Commissioner requires an audit of annual remittances exceeding USD 10,000,000, or (iv) the Registrar of Corporations issues a specific direction under the Business Corporations Act. A licensed customs brokerage house is subject to audit only upon specific regulatory direction or if its gross annual revenue exceeds USD 5,000,000.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as applied in the RMI; US GAAP may alternatively be used for non-resident entities. There is no separately codified RMI general-purpose local GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each shareholder and director must complete and sign an annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Form UBO-AR) listing all individuals with 10% or more ownership or control. The form is delivered to the registered agent, who retains it in the corporate records and confirms its correctness in the annual report. Any share transfer during the year must be accompanied by an updated UBO declaration within 14 days of the transfer.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if no audit threshold is triggered; USD 4,000 - USD 12,000 if a statutory or regulatory audit becomes mandatory

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 3% (RMI Gross Receipts Tax on RMI-source business revenue; 0% effective exemption for non-resident foreign-source income)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory exemption for non-resident domestic corporations under Section 103 of the RMI Business Corporations Act: all income derived from outside the Marshall Islands is exempt from Marshall Islands income tax and gross receipts tax. No capital gains tax, no gift or estate tax, no value added tax. If the customs brokerage is exercised through a licensed in-country presence, a flat 3% gross receipts tax may apply to gross revenue derived from RMI sources, with no tax on foreign-source revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Non-resident exempt corporations are not required to file a Marshall Islands income tax return. The only mandatory annual filing is the Corporate Annual Report (official form designator RMI MIRA/BC-AR), filed electronically through the RMI Corporate Registry portal or via the licensed registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Report must be filed on or before the anniversary date of incorporation each year. A 60-day grace period is allowed before late fees accrue; failure to file for two consecutive years exposes the corporation to administrative dissolution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name, registration number, and date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the certificate name exactly as set out in the Articles of Incorporation. No modifications are permitted without a certificate of amendment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address and registered agent name and address in the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the full street address (P.O. Box alone is not sufficient) and the name/address of the approved RMI resident registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and residential or business addresses of all directors and officers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident directors, a physical mailing address outside RMI is acceptable. Any nominee director must be disclosed with a note detailing the directorship arrangement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized and issued share capital, including number, classes, and par value; details of any redemption or restriction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident domestic corporations should list the total issued share capital and confirm that no shares have been issued to RMI residents or for RMI-source services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of tax status and any RMI business activities conducted during the reporting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Check the box for 'Non-resident exempt corporation' and certify that no taxable income was derived from sources within the Marshall Islands. If such income exists, a Gross Receipts Tax return must be filed separately.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Annual Report triggers a US$100 per month late fine, capped at US$1,000. Failure to file for two consecutive years results in automatic revocation/dissolution of the corporation. Any failure to file a required Gross Receipts Tax return (if taxable RMI-source income is discovered) carries a 25% negligence penalty plus interest at 1.5% per month, and the director/officers may be assessed personally for unpaid tax liabilities arising from fraudulent failure to disclose.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — the Republic of the Marshall Islands imposes no withholding tax on dividends paid by a domestic corporation to residents or non-residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: RMI has no comprehensive double tax agreements in force. It has a limited shipping income exemption with the United States. For foreign-source withholding taxes, a tax residency certificate can be requested from the RMI Tax and Revenue Office. To invoke any treaty relief in a treaty counterparty, the taxpayer must obtain an RMI TRC, submit a statement of residency, and provide the foreign tax authority with the TRC and details of beneficial ownership. Because RMI has no complex DTA network, no standard treaty relief process is available; double tax relief is largely unilateral and may not exist.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax rate for royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 0%. If a treaty applies (currently none for interest/royalty), the treaty rate would not be lower than the statutory rate, i.e., 0%. Domestic payments to RMI tax residents may be subject to the 3% gross receipts tax on the recipient, but no withholding is imposed at source.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 1,000,000 — Transfer pricing documentation (local country file) is compulsory for a Marshall Islands tax-resident entity that engages in controlled transactions exceeding USD 1 million in aggregate gross value. For non-resident exempt corporations, no transfer pricing documentation is required because the entity is outside RMI tax jurisdiction; but if a local customs brokerage license is held and RMI-source revenue is earned, the license holder will be subject to the 3% gross receipts tax and must maintain contemporaneous pricing records evidencing arm's length charges for customs brokerage fees.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Republic of the Marshall Islands has enacted the Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) pursuant to the Organisation of Economic Co-operation and Development / EU requirements. A non-resident domestic corporation deriving foreign-source income alone is outside the ESR scope if its tax residency is foreign or if it has no RMI-source relevant income. However, a customs brokerage house exercising a RMI license will have a taxable RMI presence and must demonstrate sufficient employees, physical office, and locally incurred operating expenditure proportionate to the customs brokerage activity. Licensees must meet the 'management and control' and 'income generated' tests or face substantial fines, strike-off, and a mandatory referral to the Financial Intelligence Unit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Gross Receipts Tax Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly claiming the non-resident exemption while earning taxable customs brokerage fees inside the Republic, and failing to file the 3% Gross Receipts Tax return. Also includes deliberately shifting RMI-source fees to foreign invoices and maintaining dual books to conceal RMI turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 50% of the tax evaded, interest at 1.5% per month, and a fine of up to $10,000 per false return. Criminal conviction for willful evasion may result in imprisonment for up to five years and a criminal fine of $30,000 per count, together with forfeiture of the proceeds of the brokerage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in or knowingly permit the filing of false declarations will be jointly and severally liable for all unpaid tax, penalties, and interest. The court may order the piercing of the corporate veil, travel bans, asset freezes, and disgorgement of personal benefits received from the evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a non-resident exempt corporation in name but maintaining a mailbox-only registered agent address and no physical office, employees, or local assets, while purportedly performing customs brokerage activities; failing to meet the Economic Substance Regulations 'relevant activity' income test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the ESR, an initial non-compliance penalty of USD 10,000, escalating to USD 20,000 for continuing default; the Registrar may strike the company off the register and notify the Tax and Revenue Office. The company's RMI banking license and customs brokerage authorizations can be suspended indefinitely.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil fines up to USD 50,000 and are disqualified from acting as directors of any RMI company for ten years. If the shell was used to launder customs duty collections, criminal liability for fraud and money laundering can attach, with imprisonment up to ten years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs Brokerage License and AML Compliance Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Acting as an unlicensed customs broker or permitting the licensed broker of record to receive cargo duty payment without a proper client due diligence file; failing to maintain suspicious transaction reporting; facilitating undervaluation or misdescription of goods to reduce import duties for clients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to USD 100,000 per transaction plus suspension/revocation of the customs broker license. The RMI Financial Intelligence Unit can impose AML monetary penalties of USD 50,000 per episode for every failure to file a Suspicious Transaction Report, and the trade passport may be revoked. Repeat offences result in a permanent banishment of the company from the RMI customs clearing system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable under the Proceeds of Crime Act for failing to maintain effective AML controls. Their personal assets can be seized, they can be named in criminal prosecutions and subjected to a travel ban, and the corporate veil will be pierced to allow creditors and customs authorities to recover unpaid duties and fines directly from individual directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Misrepresentation in Annual Report / False Beneficial Ownership Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a materially false Annual Report with the Registrar—including misstating the registered agent, directors, or share capital—or failing to disclose beneficial ownership to the RMI Registry or a licensed customs clearing partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Business Corporations Act, knowingly making a false entry in the Annual Report is punishable as perjury: a fine of up to USD 5,000 and imprisonment for up to three years. The Registrar shall also issue a dissolution order and strike the entity from the register after any verified false statement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause delivery of a false Annual Report commit statutory perjury; personal criminal liability follows regardless of the company's dissolution. The directors can incur restitution for third parties who relied on the false public record, including customs authorities or the registered agent, with personal bank accounts and travel rights restricted until full restitution.
